Socrates on morality

Socrates (c. 470/469–399 BCE) approaches morality within Socratic philosophy. Socratic method is elenchus: cooperative yet relentless cross-examination that tests definitions and reveals contradiction in moral claims. He links virtue with a kind of knowledge and suggests that wrongdoing stems from ignorance rather than clear-eyed choice. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets morality most directly—useful for searches such as “socrates quotes on morality.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Socrates thinker page for biography and to the morality theme for other voices on the same question.
